person_note: The controlling narrator is Elle Bishop, who participates throughout as I/we. Numerous quotes independently expose her in present-day scenes, interior reflection, and childhood backstory. The authorized interior excerpt confirms the same voice, while the NPR author interview explicitly states that the whole book is in Elle's first-person voice; further reviews corroborate this across its timelines and all five sections. Isolated he/she passages are unmarked because a first-person narrator can recount other characters, and the whole-book structural evidence rules against treating them as alternating third-person sections. Dialogue, aphorisms, paratext, the epigraph, and the contextless verse/fragment do not contradict the first-person base. No material uncertainty remains about the book-level person.
